purpose: Define market-specific evidence, execution semantics, trade-construction requirements and fail-closed boundaries without changing the currently locked E1 component test.
globalRules: A context proxy may influence regime classification but may not silently become the executable instrument.
No decision feature may use information published after the decision timestamp.
No market-family rule may be altered after seeing that family's sealed-holdout result.
Missing executable evidence produces WAIT, AVOID or DATA_GAP; it does not trigger a fabricated fallback.
A trade idea and an entry are separate objects: VALID_IDEA_BAD_ENTRY must be representable.
Stops are invalidation/noise models; targets are market-structure/volatility objectives; neither may be moved only to make RR pass.
High confidence is not a synonym for high heuristic score. Probability labels require out-of-sample calibration.

CRYPTO_SPOT.executionBoundary: Composite/reference history cannot imply a specific exchange fill.

CRYPTO_PERPETUAL.executionBoundary: No perpetual profitability claim without exact funding and contract-specific costs.

FX.executionBoundary: Mid/quote aggregates are not guaranteed fills; spread-side execution must be stressed.

METALS_SPOT.executionBoundary: Spot XAU/XAG quote aggregates are not exchange futures trades.

FUTURES.executionBoundary: Opaque continuous symbols are development context only; executable tests require explicit contract mapping.

US_EQUITY.clock: exchange sessions with explicit RTH/extended-hours policy
US_EQUITY.executionBoundary: Backtests must preserve corporate-action and event causality.

INDEX.executionBoundary: Index values are signals only until mapped to an executable future/ETF/CFD with its own costs and basis.

INDEX_ETF.executionBoundary: ETF fills are not interchangeable with cash-index values or futures.

preferredContext: seasonality only if predeclared and causal
ENERGY_COMMODITY_FUTURES.executionBoundary: No ETF or cash proxy may replace the underlying futures contract for executable testing.

futureIntegrationRule: These playbooks become production logic only after their features and fallbacks are individually tested under the ITE1 validation chain.
